_comment: Stealth config for @playwright/mcp, loaded by this plugin's .mcp.json via --config. PORTABLE DEFAULT: bundled Chromium + headless + JS-level stealth (realistic UA/viewport/locale, --disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled, webdriver init script) — works on headless servers. Requires 'npx playwright install chromium' once.
_maxstealth_hint: For MAXIMUM stealth on a DESKTOP with real Google Chrome + a display, set launchOptions.channel='chrome' and launchOptions.headless=false. Note: channel='chrome' fails if Chrome isn't installed; headless=false needs a display (use xvfb-run on a server).
_note: initScript MUST be a file path (relative to this config), not inline JS — inline strings crash the server with 'Init script file does not exist'.

browser._recordHar_note: COMPLETE-TRAFFIC CAPTURE: recordHar makes every MCP-driven agent session record a full HAR (all methods/frames/bodies) with no per-agent code, so interaction-triggered READ XHRs the curated map misses are still captured. WHEN IT IS WRITTEN — measured on @playwright/mcp 0.0.84 with isolated:false: ONLY when browser_close is called. A graceful shutdown (stdin closed, SIGTERM) and a kill both LOSE the segment in progress; while the browser is open the file is absent or still holds an older segment; and every browser_close OVERWRITES the file with the segment since the previous close. So the pentest commands run a checkpoint (browser_close, then har-rotate.mjs, which MOVES the file to .pentest-har/) before every ingest — never read this file directly. The path is relative to the server's CWD (the engagement root). SECRETS: the HAR holds Authorization/Cookie headers and response bodies; har-import strips header values, the raw file is gitignored and lives outside outputs/.

contextOptions.userAgent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/124.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

_clienthints_note: extraHTTPHeaders overriding Sec-Ch-Ua is a REAL stealth fix, not cosmetic. This config spoofs contextOptions.userAgent to Chrome/124 but the CLIENT HINTS still report the actual binary, so every request went out carrying Sec-Ch-Ua: "HeadlessChrome";v="<n>" while the UA claimed Chrome. WAFs block on exactly that mismatch. Established by replaying through an intercepting proxy with everything else byte-identical: no client hints -> 200, Sec-Ch-Ua=HeadlessChrome -> 403, Sec-Ch-Ua=Google Chrome -> 200. This affects ANY Akamai/Cloudflare-fronted target, so keep the three Sec-Ch-Ua headers in sync with contextOptions.userAgent whenever you bump the spoofed Chrome version — a UA/client-hint mismatch is more detectable than either value alone.
_proxy_note: launchOptions.proxy is the address CHROMIUM uses to reach the operator's intercepting proxy. It is NOT the address of the MCP server, and it is not a stealth measure: a TLS-fingerprint theory for an earlier block was tested and was WRONG — the browser reached the target fine with no proxy at all. Capture is simply the default posture here: traffic should be reviewable. HARD DEPENDENCY: while this line is set, something must be LISTENING at that address or every navigation dies with net::ERR_PROXY_CONNECTION_FAILED. TWO TOPOLOGIES, and the default matches this plugin's own: .mcp.json launches `npx @playwright/mcp` NATIVELY, so the MCP server and the Chromium it drives are host processes — the proxy is at 127.0.0.1 (macOS, Linux, WSL alike). Use host.internal (or host.docker.internal) ONLY when the MCP server itself runs inside an OrbStack/Docker container: that name is resolvable from inside a container, never on the macOS or Linux host, so it is wrong for the default launch and fails immediately. TO OVERRIDE WITHOUT EDITING THIS FILE: export PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_PROXY_SERVER=http://<host>:<port> before starting Claude Code — @playwright/mcp merges config file < environment < CLI, so the variable wins over the value above (and `--proxy-server` in .mcp.json would win over both). A RESTART IS REQUIRED EITHER WAY: the config is read once, when the MCP server starts. Editing it and retrying the navigation — the natural reflex — changes nothing; restart the MCP server (/mcp, or restart Claude Code). CHECK IT BEFORE YOU START: `node stealth/proxy-probe.mjs` TCP-connects to the configured address and tells you in one line whether the dependency is satisfied. Three independent agents on one engagement each discovered the dead proxy mid-task, from an opaque Chromium error; the probe turns that into a message you get before any work is dispatched.
_ua_note: contextOptions.userAgent + the three Sec-Ch-Ua headers are a STEALTH profile, and they lose to the engagement. A Cloudflare cf_clearance (and any UA-bound session) is issued against the exact User-Agent that solved the challenge, so a session captured in real Chrome 156 on macOS cannot be replayed by a browser claiming Chrome/124 on Linux — the values in contextOptions are simply wrong for that engagement, however good they are as a disguise. Put the session's own UA in .pentest-identities.json (`"user_agent": "<the exact UA>"`, per-identity or at the top level) and run `node stealth/ua-sync.mjs --identities .pentest-identities.json`: it writes the UA here AND regenerates all three Sec-Ch-Ua headers from it. Never change the UA alone — per _clienthints_note a UA/client-hint mismatch is MORE detectable than either value by itself, so a hand-edited UA is worse than the stock profile. ua-sync refuses to write one without the other for exactly that reason.
